paite: Siria kumpipa sepaih heutu Naaman, TOUPA'N Siriate humbitpa a azat ziak in, apu ngaih in thupi leh zahtakhuaitak ahi. Amah mihat ahi lai a, himahleh aphak hi.
heading: Naaman Hihdamna
english: Now Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honorable, because by him Yahweh had given victory to Syria; he was also a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.

paite: Siriate apawlpawl in akuankhia ua, Israel gam a pan numei naupangnou khat sal in ahon pi ua; ama'n Naaman zi nna asem hi.
english: The Syrians had gone out in bands, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little girl, and she waited on Naaman’s wife.

paite: Ama'n api kiang ah, "Samaria a om zawlnei kiang ah ka toupa va hohleh chi na ing e! Ama'n aphakna na hihdamsak ding hi a,” achi hi.
english: She said to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”

paite: Mi khat ava lut a, atoupa kiang ah, "Israel gam a numei naupangnou in huchibang khachibang in agen," chi in apu ahilh hi.
english: Someone went in and told his lord, saying, “The girl who is from the land of Israel said this.”

paite: Siria kumpipa'n, "Va hoh hen aw, Israel kumpipa kiang ah lai ka khak ding,” achi hi. Huchi in apawt a, dangkasik talent sawm leh dangka-eng khal sangguk leh silh-le-ten kikhenna ding sawm akeng hi.
english: The king of Syria said, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” He departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing.

paite: Huai laikhak Israel kumpipa ava pia a, huai ah hiai akigelh hi, “Hiai lai na mu dia, ngai in, ka sikha Naaman aphakna na hihdamsak ding in na kiang ah ka hon sawl hi,” chih.
english: He brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “Now when this letter has come to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy.”

paite: Israel kumpipa'n huai lai asim a, hichi ahong hi a, apuan abotkek a, "Mite that thei a, hingsak nawn thei Pathian hia ka hih? Hiai mi in phak hihdam dia ka kiang ah ahon sawl mawkmawk. Ngaihtuah unla, ka tung ah thusia azong hi, chih thei dih ua," achi hi.
english: When the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to heal a man of his leprosy? But please consider and see how he seeks a quarrel against me.”

paite: Pathian mipa Elisha in Israel kumpipa'n apuan abotkek chih ana zak in, hichi ahong hi a, "Bangziak a na puan botkek na hia? Ka kiang ah hong paileh ake, huchi in Israel gam ah zawlnei a-om chih athei mai ding," va chi ding in kumpipa kiang ah mi asawl hi.
english: It was so, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

paite: Huchi in asakolte leh akangtalaite toh Naaman ava hoh a, Elisha inn kongbul ah ava dingh hi.
english: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariots, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.

paite: Elisha in, "Jordan lui ah sagihvei va kisil inla, na sa in ngeina apu nawn dia, huchi in na siangta ding," chi ding in mi asawl hi.
english: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh shall come again to you, and you shall be clean.”

paite: Himahleh, Naaman aheh mahmah a, apaikhia a, “Ngai un, amah mah ka kiang a hong pawt dia, ahong dingh dia, TOUPA a Pathian min asam dia, ka phakna tung ah akhut akoih dia, ka phak damsak ding ei ve, chi mah hi veng in," achi hi.
english: But Naaman was angry, and went away and said, “Behold, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’

paite: "Israel gam lui tengteng sang in Damaskas kho luite, Abana leh Pharpar ahoihzaw kei a hia? Huaite a kisil in ka siangthou thei kei dia hia?" achi hi. Huchi in akilehhei a, heh mahmah in apai hi.
english: Aren’t Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn’t I wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in a rage.

paite: Asikhate'n ava naih ua, ava houpih ua, "Ka pa aw, zawlnei in thil haksatak hon hihsak dekleh leng na hihmai kei dia hia? Va kisil inla, hong siangthou in, achih pen hih zawk tuak lua hilou maw?" achi uhi.
english: His servants came near and spoke to him, and said, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?”

paite: Huchi in ahohsuk a, Pathian mipa gen bang in Jordan lui ah sagihvei ava kidiah a; huchi in asa naungek sa bang ahong hi nawn a, ahong siangta hi.
english: Then went he down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

paite: Amah leh aheute tengteng Pathian mipa kiang ah akik nawn ua, ama ah ava dingh uhi. Ama'n, "Ngai in, Israel ah lou ngal leitung tengteng ah Pathian ana om kei, chih ka theita. Huaiziak in tu in na sikha vualzawlna la ding in ka hon ngen," achi hi.
english: He returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him; and he said, “See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel. Now therefore, please take a gift from your servant.”

paite: Himahleh ama'n, "Akiang a ka omna TOUPA ahin bang in ka gen ahi. Bangmah ka la kei ding," achi hi. Huchi in ama'n la ding in angen a; himahleh ala ut kei bikbek hi.
english: But he said, “As Yahweh lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none.” He urged him to take it; but he refused.

paite: Naaman in, "Ahihkeileh, kei na sikha sabiltung nih puak khop leitang hon lasak in. Tuban siah kei na sikha in TOUPA kiang kia ah ngal lou halmang thillat leh kithoihna himhim pathian dangte kiang ah ka lan nawn het kei ding hi.
english: Naaman said, “If not, then, please let two mules’ load of earth be given to your servant; for your servant will from now on offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, but to Yahweh.

paite: Hiai thil ah TOUPA'N na sikha ngaidam hen. Rimmon inn a be dia ka ban a kingai a ka toupa alut chiang a, kei leng ka kun sam angaih chiang in TOUPA'N hon ngaidam hen," achi hi.
english: In this thing may Yahweh pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon. When I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, may Yahweh pardon your servant in this thing.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Lungmuangtak in pai in," achi hi. Huchi in akiang a pan apawt a, gamla lou apaikhe man hi.
english: He said to him, “Go in peace.” So he departed from him a little way.

paite: Himahleh Pathian mipa Elisha sikha Gehazi in, "Ngai in, ka pu in Siria mi Naaman thil hon tawite la het lou in apaisak mawk a. TOUPA ahin bang in ka gen ahi, ka va delh dia, aneih banghiam bek ka va la ding," achi hi.
english: But Gehazi the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Behold, my master has spared this Naaman the Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought. As Yahweh lives, I will run after him, and take something from him.”

paite: Huchi in Gehazi in Naaman adelhta hi. Naaman in kuahiam in adelh amuh in, na houpih ding in kangtalai a pan akumkhia a, "Hoih vek na maw?" achi hi.
english: So Gehazi followed after Naaman. When Naaman saw one running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him, and said, “Is all well?”

paite: Ama'n, "Hoih vek mah e. Ka pu in, ngai in, tu mah in Ephraim tanggam a pan in zawlneite tapate lak a tangval nih ka kiang ah ahong ahong ua, amaute dangkasik talent khat leh puansilh kikhenna ding nih pia in, chih gen ding in ahong sawl hi," achi hi.
english: He said, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, even now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.’”

paite: Naaman in, "Khamuang inla, talent nih la ve," achi hi. Huchi in la ding in angen a, dangkasik talent nih puansilh kikhenna ding nih toh ip nih ah athun a, asikhate nih aposak a, ama ah apaipihta uhi.
english: Naaman said, “Be pleased to take two talents.” He urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and laid them on two of his servants; and they carried them before him.

paite: Tang ava tun un alaksak a, insung ah akoih a; huchi in mite apaisakta hi.
english: When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand, and stored them in the house. Then he let the men go, and they departed.

paite: Amah alut a, apu ma ah ava dingh hi. Elisha in akiang ah, "Koi a hong kipan na hia, Gehazi?” achi hi. Ama'n, "Na sikha koimah ah ka hoh kei," achi hi.
english: But he went in, and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “Where did you come from, Gehazi?” He said, “Your servant went nowhere.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Nang mu dia kangtalai a pan huai mi ahong kum lai in ka lungtang na kiang ah apai kei maw? Sum, puansilhte, olive huante, grephuante, belamte, bawngtalte, sikhapate leh sikhanute lak hun ahi a hia?
english: He said to him, “Didn’t my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and cattle, and male servants and female servants?

paite: Huaiziak in Naaman phak nang ah abelh dia, tangtawn in na suante ah leng abelh ding," achi hi. Huchi in a-omna a pan vuk bang a ngou in phaksa in apaikheta hi.
english: Therefore the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and to your offspring forever.” He went out from his presence a leper, as white as snow.
